ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, there is a uniform magnetic field region in space with a direction perpendicular to the plane of the paper. The distance between the upper and lower edges of the magnetic field is $h=5.2\mathrm{m}$, and the magnetic induction intensity is $B=1\mathrm{T}$. A square wire frame with side length $L=1\mathrm{m}$, resistance $R{=}1\Omega$, and mass $m{=}1\mathrm{kg}$ is initially at rest and falls from the upper edge of the magnetic field region. When the $PQ$ side of the coil reaches the lower edge of the magnetic field, it just begins to move at a constant velocity. The gravitational acceleration is $g{=}10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. The velocity $v$ when the edge $PQ$ moves to the lower edge of the magnetic field.
2. The Joule heat generated by a wire frame passing through a magnetic field
3. The time it takes for the wire frame to fall from the start until the edge $PQ$ reaches the lower edge of the magnetic field.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are two blue horizontal dashed lines in the figure, representing the upper and lower boundaries of the magnetic-field region; between the two dashed lines are drawn multiple “×”, indicating a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the paper surface inward. On the right side, a vertical double-headed arrow marks that the spacing between the upper and lower boundaries is h. A square wire frame is located at the upper boundary, with side length labeled L, upper side MN, and lower side PQ; initially side PQ is exactly at the upper boundary of the magnetic field, and the wire frame enters the magnetic field downward. Reasoning: According to the method given in the problem, divide the process into three stages: entering the magnetic field, completely in the magnetic field, and leaving the magnetic field. Let k=B^2L^2/R. From B=1 T, L=1 m, R=1 Ω, obtain k=1 N·s/m. 1. When PQ reaches the lower boundary and has just begun to leave the magnetic field and moves at constant speed, the magnetic-field resistance balances gravity: mg=kv=(B^2L^2/R)v. Therefore v=mgR/(B^2L^2)=1×10×1/(1^2×1^2)=10 m/s. 2. From the start until PQ reaches the lower boundary, the wire frame falls a height h, gravity does work mgh, part of which is transformed into kinetic energy and part into the Joule heat Q_entry in the entering stage; when completely inside the magnetic field, the magnetic flux does not change, and no Joule heat is produced. Thus mgh=1/2 mv^2+Q_entry, Q_entry=1×10×5.2-1/2×1×10^2=52-50=2 J. Afterward the wire frame completely leaves the magnetic field at constant speed, falls a distance L, the kinetic energy is unchanged, and all the work done by gravity is transformed into Joule heat: mgL=1×10×1=10 J. Therefore the total Joule heat Q=Q_entry+mgL=2+10=12 J. 3. Let the speed when the wire frame has just completely entered the magnetic field be v1. It moves a distance h-L=5.2-1=4.2 m completely in the magnetic field, with no induced current, and undergoes free-fall acceleration, so v^2=v1^2+2g(h-L). Substituting v=10 m/s gives 100=v1^2+2×10×4.2=v1^2+84, so v1=4 m/s. Integrate momentum for the entering stage: mv1=mg t1-kL, namely 1×4=10t1-1×1, giving t1=0.5 s. The stage completely in the magnetic field has t2=(v-v1)/g=(10-4)/10=0.6 s. Total time t=t1+t2=0.5+0.6=1.1 s.
